abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a novel hierarchical semantics for intuitionistic modal logics based on neighborhood frames with reflection principles. Traditional Kripke semantics fail to capture certain constructive aspects of modality essential for computer science applications. We develop an alternative framework termed reflective neighborhood semantics (RNS), wherein each world is equipped with a self-referential neighborhood function satisfying coherence axioms. The central contribution establishes a precise correspondence between extensions of intuitionistic propositional logic with modal operators and first-order definable classes of RNS frames. We demonstrate that this semantics resolves previously observed gaps in the known intuitionistic modal cube by providing sound and complete axiomatizations for six previously uncharacterized logics. The proof employs a novel filtration technique adapted to reflective neighborhoods, yielding a decidability result for the satisfiability problem in these logics. Furthermore, we show that RNS admits a natural categorical interpretation, connecting to topos-theoretic foundations of constructive mathematics. This work opens new avenues for investigating the computational content of intuitionistic modality and establishes a paradigm for extending the BHK interpretation to modal reasoning. The framework's flexibility suggests applications in specification logics for concurrent systems and intuitionistic epistemic reasoning.

We present a substantially strengthened analysis of the proof-theoretic strength of the Łukasiewicz logic Ł, establishing exact ordinal bounds that improve upon classical results by Lev Barton and John Bell. The standard approach to ordinal assignment for continuous t-norm logics relies on semantic interpretations via MV-algebras and their state spaces. Our method introduces a refined version of the takesaki-dedekind theorem adapted to linearly ordered commutative residuated lattices, enabling sharper measurability arguments. We prove that the proof-theoretic ordinal of Ł is exactly ω^ω, significantly improving the previous bound of ω^ω·2 and resolving a long-standing open problem in algebraic logic. The proof proceeds by constructing a novel ordinal notation system for the free one-generator algebra in the variety of MV-algebras, employing a combinatorial analysis of the subdirectly irreducible components. As a corollary, we obtain refined results on the definability of multiplication in the real unit interval under the standard Łukasiewicz t-norm, demonstrating that multiplication is not ⌢Σ1-definable without additional set-theoretic assumptions. These results have immediate implications for the complexity of satisfiability in Łukasiewicz logic and the structural description of free MV-algebras.

We introduce Λ-Prolog, a dependently-typed logical framework designed for mechanizing proof search in higher-order intuitionistic logic with inductive and coinductive definitions. Unlike traditional proof assistants based on type theory, Λ-Prolog treats the operational semantics of unification and backtracking as first-class logical concepts, enabling direct specification of search procedures within the logical framework itself. The system architecture comprises three components: (i) a core type theory extending the Calculus of Inductive Constructions with hereditary Harrop formulas, (ii) a polymorphic unification algorithm with occurs-check optimization, and (iii) a programmable proof search primitive supporting both depth-first and iterative deepening strategies. We establish the soundness and completeness of our proof search primitives with respect to Kripke semantics for the underlying logic. The paper includes extensive formal verification of representative theorems from reverse mathematics and constructive analysis, demonstrating significant speedup compared to naive proof search in Agda. A distinctive feature of Λ-Prolog is its support for hypothetical judgments and embedded implications, enabling direct representation of context-dependent reasoning in mathematical proofs. The framework naturally accommodates abduction, theorem proving under assumptions, and explanation generation, positioning it as a versatile tool for automated mathematical reasoning research.

We present substantial enhancements to the Imandra proof assistant, specifically addressing the verification of dynamical systems specified via ordinary differential equations. Previous work on hybrid systems verification in Imandra encountered severe performance bottlenecks when reasoning about state trajectories exceeding moderate time horizons. This paper introduces two complementary techniques: (i) an optimized differential induction principle exploiting symmetries in the vector field, and (ii) a compositional verification pipeline enabling decomposition of complex system invariants into independently verifiable components. The differential induction principle employs a novel variant of Keplerian averaging that reduces the computational complexity of invariant strengthening from exponential to polynomial in the number of state variables. Our compositional pipeline integrates with Imandra's existing counterexample generation infrastructure, providing diagnostic information when component-level verification fails. We demonstrate the practical effectiveness of these improvements through extensive benchmarks on the standard suite of hybrid systems benchmarks maintained by NASA Langley. Results indicate a mean speedup of 47× for trajectory verification queries with horizons exceeding 100 time units, with no degradation in the precision of safety guarantees. The enhanced system has been successfully applied to formal verification of autonomous vehicle controllers and neural network controlled systems, where previous methods were impractical.
